t: Paragraph (5) of section 404(a) of such Act is amended by inserting “second” immediately before “preceding”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that inserts the word "second" before "preceding" in an existing statutory paragraph. There is no tempting reading: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely technical amendment to statutory text, changing a word from 'preceding' to 'second preceding'. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. It is a legislative drafting change with no procedural impact on participation.
qwen_block.s: Paragraph (5) of section 404(a) of such Act is amended by inserting “second” immediately before “preceding”.

opus.w: This section only inserts the word "second" before "preceding" in an existing paragraph. It does not mention any party outside the federal government, and it does not create a consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Nothing in the text is even on-topic for participation.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** No reading here plausibly counts as participation. This is a technical amendment: it adds the word "second" before "preceding" in section 404(a)(5). It names no outside party, no consultation, no hearing, no comment period, no rulemaking authority and no right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statutory time reference. It does not establish any process for consultation, comment, or coordination with entities outside the federal government. There are no actors involved other than the legislative text itself.
qwen_chat.s: Paragraph (5) of section 404(a) of such Act is amended by inserting “second” immediately before “preceding”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a statute could implicitly change participation requirements elsewhere, but this specific text is merely a technical amendment to a time reference ("second preceding") and contains no language regarding consultation, hearings, comments, or outside involvement. It fails the definition because it does not involve any party outside the federal government in a decision-making process.
